test_title: PYST 23: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I - GA (Held On: 14 Jun, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Globalisation refers to the integration of economies worldwide. Which of the following was a major globalisation strategy adopted by the Indian government in 1991?

options.text: Reducing trade barriers and encouraging foreign investment

solution:
The correct answer is __**Reducing trade barriers and encouraging foreign investment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In 1991, India adopted economic liberalization policies under the New Economic Policy to combat a severe balance-of-payments crisis.
 
• The government reduced trade barriers, lowered import tariffs, and encouraged foreign direct investment (FDI).
 
• This globalization strategy aimed to integrate India into the global economy by promoting exports and attracting foreign capital.
 
• The reforms included deregulation of industries, privatization of state-owned enterprises, and opening sectors to private and foreign investors.
 
• These measures marked the beginning of India's transition towards a market-oriented economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Globalization:**

 
 
• Refers to the process of integration of economies, cultures, and societies on a global scale.
 
• It involves free movement of goods, services, capital, and labor across borders.
 
• Globalization accelerates technological exchange and promotes international trade and investment.
 
 
 
• **Balance-of-Payments Crisis (1991):**
 
 
• India faced a severe economic crisis in 1991 due to dwindling foreign exchange reserves.
 
• The reserves were insufficient to cover imports for more than two weeks.
 
• The crisis led to major economic reforms under Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao and Finance Minister Dr. Manmohan Singh.
 
 
 
• **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI):**
 
 
• FDI refers to investment by a company or individual based in one country into businesses located in another country.
 
• FDI was encouraged in India post-1991 reforms to boost industrial growth and generate employment.
 
 
 
• **Trade Liberalization:**
 
 
• Involves reducing tariffs, quotas, and regulations on international trade.
 
• India's trade liberalization policies aimed to make domestic industries competitive globally.
